content.title: NHL overtime: How does it work? Regular season and postseason rules explained
content.text: The NHL regular season is almost here, with pre-season games now well underway ahead of the October start, and DAZN is THE place to watch all the NHL action unfold.DAZN is the new home of the NHL, streaming every game of the 2025/26 season exclusively internationally, beginning on Tuesday, October 7, when the two-time defending Stanley Cup Champions, the Florida Panthers, have their banner night as they host the Chicago Blackhawks. With the Stanley Cup Playoffs and Finals included, that's over 1,300 games available live* and on demand on DAZN .In addition, subscribers can enjoy features such as home and away commentary selection and access to NHL programming, including Puck Personalities and Mic Drop.Ultimate customers can also enjoy enhanced broadcast features and a discount at NHLShop.com. What happens if the Panthers and Blackhawks go overtime? DAZN News provides all of that information for you below on how the overtime work and what is different if anything when the Stanley Cup Playoffs begin? Sign up for NHL.TV on DAZN now to watch the full season What are the rules of overtime during the NHL regular season and Stanley Cup Playoffs?An NHL game lasts 60 minutes, broken up into three periods of 20 minutes each. After the first two periods, there is an intermission. If the game is tied after the third period, then the game has a five-minute sudden-death overtime. The first team to score wins the game. If neither team scores a goal, you then go to a shootout. Each team is given three shots. Whoever scores the most goals within those shots is the winner. If it is tied, the shootout will go to a sudden-death format.The rules are a little different during the Stanley Cup Playoffs. If the game is tied after three periods, there is a 15-minute intermission. Then, the game resumes, where overtime will be conducted in 20-minute periods. There is no shootout if the game remains tied. You play as many overtime periods as possible until a team scores a goal to win the game.
